title: Ship iPhone and Android apps from one coding agent
promise: Build, run and test on both platforms from Claude Code or Codex, starting with Apple's Xcode MCP and Google's Android CLI.

items.why: Lets Claude Code or Codex modify and build the project you have open in Xcode, through Xcode's own MCP server.
Tests the build on a real iPhone over USB: opens the app, reads the screen, taps, swipes and types.
Covers Android from one command line: sets up the SDK, scaffolds the project, and builds and runs it on a device or emulator.
When a build breaks, finds fixes other agents have validated, and reports back whether the fix worked.

title: A research analyst in five tools
promise: Search the web and the literature, read what you find, run the numbers and write it up.

items.why: Runs plain-language web searches and deep research tasks that come back ranked, structured and cited.
Finds the papers: searches Semantic Scholar, arXiv and PubMed, follows citations and pulls open-access full text. No API key.
Reads the PDFs, Word, PowerPoint and Excel files you collect, keeping tables and reading order, and hands them over as Markdown.
Runs the analysis code in an isolated cloud sandbox, in Python, JavaScript or shell.
Writes up the findings as Notion pages and database entries your team can read.

title: No-key MCP starter pack
promise: Six MCP servers that need no account or API key: a browser, current docs, real code examples, file conversion, spreadsheets and diagrams.

items.why: Drives a browser through accessibility snapshots, so your assistant can navigate, click and fill forms without a vision model.
Puts current, version-specific library docs and examples into the context, instead of what the model remembers.
Shows how an API is used in practice, searching millions of public GitHub repositories by literal string or regex.
Turns PDFs, Office files, images and audio into Markdown your assistant can read.
Creates, reads and edits Excel workbooks, with formulas, formatting and charts, without Excel installed.
Draws architecture and flow diagrams from XML, CSV or Mermaid, and opens them in the draw.io editor.

title: Run a team of coding agents
promise: Keep several coding agents working at once: see which need you, keep their work apart, hand off between them and review before you push.

items.why: Shows which of your Claude Code, Codex, Pi or OpenCode sessions are working, finished or waiting for you, in one terminal.
Gives each agent its own container on its own git branch, so they can work in parallel without conflicts.
Passes work from one agent to the next with a handoff that says where it stopped, what failed and what is still open.
Reviews each agent's changes before you push, with scanners and a separate Claude Code or Codex reviewer.

title: A realtime voice agent
promise: The four parts of an agent you talk to: a realtime framework, speech recognition, a fast model and a voice.

items.why: Runs the conversation: streams audio over WebRTC, detects when the speaker is done, and chains speech-to-text, the model and text-to-speech.
Hears the user, with real-time streaming transcription and speaker diarization.
Thinks fast: serves open-weight models such as Qwen and GPT OSS through an OpenAI-compatible API, built for very fast inference.
Answers out loud with low-latency text-to-speech, in a custom voice cloned from a short sample.

title: Watch your agents in production
promise: Trace every call, see what each request costs, and send the errors back to your coding agent.

items.why: Traces every LLM, retriever and tool call on OpenTelemetry and scores them with LLM-as-judge evaluations. Runs locally.
Logs each request's prompt, cost and latency through a one-line proxy, and caches repeated completions to cut spend.
Brings production errors back to your coding agent: issues, stack traces, distributed traces and Sentry's root-cause analysis.
